evidence_against: At 24h and 72h, BTC and ETH prices rose while both open interest and long/short ratios declined. This weakens a straightforward interpretation of the move as broad, fresh leveraged accumulation.
BTC and ETH depth20 quote-notional imbalances were negative despite positive taker quote imbalances. Resting displayed depth therefore did not confirm the direction implied by aggressive flow.

The 12h horizon differs materially from the longer horizons: BTC and ETH open interest increased over its 7-hour actual span, whereas open interest declined over the 19-hour and 67-hour spans. This makes leverage interpretation horizon-sensitive.
The 12h, 24h, and 72h horizons have actual spans of 7, 19, and 67 hours rather than their nominal durations, and the 1h horizon is unavailable; fine sequencing cannot be established.

Liquidation data indicate substantial short liquidations but are explicitly lower-bound aggregates from an unverified, potentially truncated legacy REST source, so they cannot conclusively establish the role of short covering.
evidence_for: The coherent common direction across available 12h, 24h, and 72h horizons is positive BTC, ETH, and ETHBTC returns, accompanied by declining BTC and ETH long/short ratios.
Breadth improved from 75 to 79 advancers and decliners fell from 8 to 6 between captures, aligning cross-sectional participation with the positive price-return family.

ETH outperformed BTC across all three available horizons, and direct ETHBTC closed above 0.03 for 13 consecutive hourly observations. This corroborates the relative-strength portion of the price family.
Positive spot taker quote imbalance for BTC and ETH is directionally consistent with the positive return and breadth observations, although it conflicts with negative displayed depth imbalance.

The strongest coherent interpretation is a broad upward impulse with ETH-relative strength, in which declining long/short ratios, longer-horizon open-interest contraction, and reported short liquidations are consistent with at least some deleveraging or short-covering contribution rather than unambiguously new leveraged participation.
hypotheses: Conflict interpretation only: available evidence supports a mixed-mechanism advance—positive price, breadth, ETH-relative performance, and aggressive flow coexist with negative displayed depth and deleveraging/position-ratio signals.

Strongest falsification: if the return/breadth signal were principally an artifact of short covering or transient aggressive flow, subsequent observations would fail to retain broad participation and relative ETH strength while the leverage and order-book families continue to diverge. No such subsequent evidence is supplied here.

An alternative falsification of the deleveraging/short-covering interpretation is that the positive 12h open-interest changes reflect renewed position building; however, their 7-hour actual span conflicts with the 19-hour and 67-hour open-interest declines and is insufficient to resolve the mechanism.
summary: Detected disagreement is concentrated between the consistently positive price/breadth/ETH-relative family and the mixed derivatives/microstructure family. The most coherent reading is a broad upside impulse with ETH leadership that may be partly propelled by position unwinding or short covering. The strongest challenge is that the leverage evidence changes sign across imperfect horizon spans, while liquidation completeness and subsequent confirmation are unavailable; the mechanism remains unresolved and non-canonical.
uncertainties: The conflict router identifies multi-horizon signal-family disagreement but supplies no adjudication authority or canonical market state.
No valid 1h anchor is available, preventing assessment of the immediate ordering between price, open interest, long/short ratio, and microstructure changes.
The nominal 12h, 24h, and 72h windows span 7, 19, and 67 actual hours respectively.
Long/short ratio declines are supplied without a decomposition of changes in longs versus shorts.

Depth20 imbalance and taker imbalance measure different aspects of market microstructure and are point-in-time or short-sample measures; their disagreement does not identify which side will dominate next.
Liquidation aggregates are lower bounds with unknown pagination truncation and unverified source completeness.
Macro fields are absent in the latest capture, and no broader rotation sensors such as BTC dominance, Total2, Total3, or stablecoin dominance are supplied.
